newsitem.title: MEXICO: Hylsamex to invest $220 mln over two yrs.
newsitem.headline: Hylsamex to invest $220 mln over two yrs.

text.p: Steelmaker Hylsamex plans to invest $220 million over the next two years, mainly on a second line at its mini-mill, a company director said Friday.
"The company has plans to invest $220 million in plant and expansion in 1997 and 1998," director of investment relations Othon Diaz said in a telephone interview.
Hylsamex is a flat steel maker and the principal subsidiary of industrial conglomerate Grupo Alfa.
Most of the investment will be channelled into the second stage of Hylsamex's mini-mill, Diaz said.
"Mini-mill output will grow by 750,000 tonnes, but operation is such that capacity to produce flat steel will increase by 500,000 tonnes," he added.
Hylsamex also plans to increase production of hot-rolled products by 180,000 tonnes per year, and to raise output of galvanized steel by 120,000 tonnes in its subsidiary Galvak, Diaz said.
The company is still considering a stock placement to raise $100 million towards its investment plans, Diaz said.

"As yet I know nothing concrete about the stock placement. One of the forms considered and seen as desireable is for Hylsamex to place stock on the market and the chairman has mentioned the figure of $100 million several times," he said.
Hylsamex also intended to contract loans with banks like the U.S. Export-Import Bank to acquire machinery, but also had in-house resources to draw on.
"I can't give a figure for in-house resources...but (they) are enough, with Eximbank financing and the share offer, to keep the company's finances healthy," Diaz said.
